metadata.description: Seven plugins for coding sessions: solo-skills (every skill that stands alone, in one install), code-desk (repo standards, planning, and status comms), diagrams (structural diagrams), atelier (tiered delegation agents and session-discipline hooks), kaneo (work tracked on a live Kaneo board), obsidian-toolkit (Obsidian plugin development), and plugin-feedback (report a plugin defect without leaving the session).

plugins.description: Audit a repo against a documented structure standard, scaffold the gaps, then plan, track, and report the work that follows: conformant issues, source-grounded plans, meta-structure and memory upkeep, board triage, recurring status comms, and themed PowerPoint decks.
plugins.name: code-desk

plugins.description: Structural diagrams for repo docs, decks, and briefings, with consistent SVG and PNG output: Mermaid for GitHub-rendered markdown, Python diagrams for cloud architecture with provider icons, draw.io reading and headless export, Excalidraw sketches, and raw Graphviz. Data charts belong to the dataviz skill, deck theming to pptx-themes.
plugins.name: diagrams

plugins.description: Delegate work to model-tiered agents instead of doing it all in one session: size the task, pick a delegation architecture, and dispatch scoped slices to scouts, builders, reviewers, and managers. Skills cover orchestration, session handoff, backlog waves, and a review cycle that runs before work lands. Hooks watch the context watermark, keep the handoff fresh and surface it on cold start, isolate writing workers in their own git worktrees, and hold protected config in custody. Run /atelier:activate to arm it in a project and see what each hook resolved.
plugins.name: atelier

plugins.description: Track a repo's work on a live Kaneo board instead of in-repo task files, so parallel sessions stop claiming the same task and no branch grows its own backlog. Ships the workflow skill, the board's MCP server definition, a reference manager agent, and hooks that keep claim authority in the root session, block board writes while the config is incomplete, catch a stray MCP registration that would silently authenticate the owner instead of the agent, and stamp every write with its agent and session. Configure with five KANEO_* env vars; nothing about an instance is baked in.
plugins.name: kaneo

plugins.description: Build Obsidian plugins against the real API — lifecycle, settings, vault operations, commands, chat and copilot sidebar UIs, in-plugin MCP servers over Streamable HTTP — and automate vaults from the terminal with the official Obsidian CLI.
plugins.name: obsidian-toolkit

plugins.description: File a bug or feature request against a plugin you are using without leaving the session. Hooks tell the primary session and its dispatched workers what each may file, and a stdlib reporter writes the issue to a fixed template instead of a free-handed gh call.
plugins.name: plugin-feedback

plugins.description: Every skill that stands on its own, in one install instead of a shelf of one-skill plugins: harness and environment config, session discipline, research, diagrams and data visualization, repo and project setup, planning, comms, and Obsidian plugin development. Membership is derived, not curated — a gate re-reads the skill bodies every run and keeps out anything that needs a companion agent or hook.
plugins.name: solo-skills
